title: How do you prepare training evidence for an ISO certification audit?
description: How certification auditors test clause 7.2 competence, based on ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group guidance, with a checklist of evidence for any ISO standard.
shortAnswer: To prepare training evidence for an ISO certification audit, show that you determined the competence each role needs, took actions such as training to achieve it, evaluated whether those actions worked, and retained appropriate documented information as evidence. Auditors following ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group guidance sample people in every process, interview and observe them, and treat attendance records alone as insufficient proof of competence. The same clause 7.2 logic applies across ISO management system standards.
keyTakeaways: Clause 7.2 competence follows the same harmonized structure in ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 45001, and other management system standards, so the evidence approach carries across.
The ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group says competence should be evaluated within all processes, not as an isolated requirement owned by human resources.
Auditors are guided to assess how competence needs are determined, how actions are chosen, and how effectiveness is evaluated, then verify documented evidence for sampled people.
The guidance states that course participation alone does not necessarily show a person is competent, because it may show only that knowledge was gained, not applied.
ISO 9001:2026 was published on September 16, 2026; ISO lists no change to clause 7.2 among its main changes, and certified organizations have three years to transition.

sections.heading: What do certification auditors look at for training?

blocks.text: Certification auditors look at whether your organization has a systematic way to identify the competence it needs and whether its approach to acquiring and using competent people is effective. The most detailed public description of how they do this is the [ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group](https://committee.iso.org/home/tc176/iso-9001-auditing-practices-group.html) (APG) paper on auditing competence, written by experts from ISO Technical Committee 176 and the International Accreditation Forum (IAF).

According to the [APG competence paper](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-Competence.pdf) (edition 2, June 2022), the auditor should be able to:

items: assess the process for determining competences;
observe whether competences were appropriately determined;
review how actions to achieve those competences are identified and provided; and
review how the effectiveness of those actions is evaluated.

blocks.text: The paper also says that "competence should be evaluated within all QMS processes and not as an isolated set of requirements in a specific process," and that audit team members should share what they find about competence in their daily meetings. The APG notes its papers are guidance, not requirements, and have not been endorsed by ISO or the IAF.

sections.heading: How do auditors test competence in practice?

blocks.text: Auditors sample people at work, interview them, and observe whether they can do what their role requires, then check the documented evidence for those people. The APG paper lists the opportunities an auditor should have when auditing production or service provision:

items: Obtain information on necessary competences by interviewing process leaders or others who define requirements, such as human resources, and by reviewing documented competence information.
Observe the performance of persons against objectives and job expectations.
Interview a sample of those persons to evaluate whether they are aware of the competence requirements for their activities.
Confirm whether these persons are able to perform their duties.
Verify that when the usual people are absent, others with adequate competence are available to replace them.

blocks.title: Why attendance is not enough
blocks.text: The APG competence paper states that training records can verify a course was completed, "but a participation at the course alone does not necessarily provide evidence that the trainee is competent, as it may only demonstrate that knowledge was gained, not necessarily that it is being effectively applied."

The APG paper on [evidence collection](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-EvidenceCollection.pdf) adds that audit evidence is generally based on samples, that objective evidence does not necessarily depend on documented information except where the standard requires it, and that it is the organization's responsibility to provide objective evidence of conformity. Clause 7.2 is one of the places where documented information is required.

sections.heading: What evidence satisfies each part of clause 7.2?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2 has four parts: determine necessary competence, ensure people are competent on the basis of education, training, or experience, take actions and evaluate their effectiveness, and retain appropriate documented information as evidence. The APG paper's competence cycle gives examples for each. The table below is an original mapping built from it.

blocks.caption: Clause 7.2 evidence map (illustrative)
head: Clause 7.2 element
Examples the APG paper gives
What an auditor may test
rows: Job descriptions, job evaluation, job analysis, or a verbal description
Whether competence needs were updated for new processes, products, technology, or contracts
Training, hiring, on the job training, mentoring, reassigning, adjusting the job, subcontracting
Whether the action chosen fits the gap and the risk
Observation of performance, examination of results of tasks and projects, tests
Whether sampled people can actually perform, and whether deficiencies were acted on
Diplomas, licenses, resumes, completion of training, performance reviews
Evidence of how each sampled person was deemed competent
Continuing professional development, appraisals, inspection or audit of work, refresher prompts for qualification revalidation
Whether a monitoring process exists and is acted on
Competence requirements communicated to suppliers by contract, order, or other means
Whether outsourced work, including outsourced training, is done by competent people

blocks.text: The APG paper notes that clause 7.2 d) requires "appropriate" documented information and that the word gives organizations leeway to decide what has value. It also cautions auditors against raising findings that documented information is needed without first considering the existing competence of personnel. The broader concept is covered in [evidence of competence](/glossary/evidence-of-competence).

sections.heading: When is training evidence reviewed in the certification cycle?

blocks.text: Training evidence is checked mainly at stage 2 of an initial certification audit and again at surveillance and recertification audits. The APG paper on the [two stage initial certification audit](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-2stage.pdf) describes stage 1 as primarily for scoping, planning, and judging readiness, including whether the client has prepared and is using necessary documentation and whether internal audits and management reviews are planned and performed.

If stage 1 shows the management system is lacking, the APG says the certification body should inform the organization formally so it can fix deficiencies before stage 2. A competence process with no evaluation of effectiveness, or a training matrix that does not match the processes in scope, is worth fixing at that point.

sections.heading: What should be ready before the audit?

items: A competence requirement for every role that affects the management system, at a level of detail suited to its risk. The [training matrix guide](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) shows one structure.
Evidence of education, training, or experience for each person, including qualifications required by law for specific functions, such as licensed trades or clinicians.
Records of actions taken to close competence gaps, and how their effectiveness was evaluated (observation, work review, tests), not only attendance.
A cross training or deputy chart for critical tasks, since auditors may check cover when usual staff are absent.
Competence requirements in contracts with external providers, including outsourced training.
Internal audit and corrective action records that show competence gaps were found and fixed.

For ISO/IEC 27001, awareness and training evidence under clause 7.3 and Annex A control 6.3; for ISO 45001, evidence that workers can identify hazards. See the [ISO/IEC 27001](/regulations/iso-27001-awareness-training-requirements) and [ISO 45001](/regulations/iso-45001-competence-and-awareness) pages.

sections.heading: Does the ISO 9001:2026 revision change training evidence?

blocks.text: Not materially for clause 7.2. ISO published ISO 9001:2026 on September 16, 2026, retaining the harmonized structure, and ISO's summary of main changes lists new awareness requirements on quality culture and ethical behavior in clause 7.3 but no change to clause 7.2. Organizations certified to ISO 9001:2015 have three years to move to the new edition. The APG papers were written for ISO 9001:2015. Details are on the [ISO 9001 competence page](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines the competence each role needs as a structured framework, links it to training and assessment items, and records how each person's competence was evaluated, which matches the determine, act, evaluate, and retain cycle an ISO auditor follows. See [standards and accreditation](/platform/standards-accreditation) and [verification and trust](/platform/verification-trust).

faqs.q: Does ISO require a training matrix?
faqs.a: No ISO management system standard names a training matrix. Clause 7.2 requires you to determine necessary competence and retain appropriate documented information. A matrix is a common way to show this, but the APG notes that documentation can range from competence databases to a verbal explanation, depending on context and risk.

faqs.q: Will the auditor interview frontline staff about their training?
faqs.a: Usually yes. APG guidance describes interviewing a sample of people to evaluate whether they are aware of the competence requirements for their activities and confirming they can perform their duties. Sampling, observing, and interviewing personnel is described as a key audit activity for reaching valid conclusions about competence.

faqs.q: Is a certificate from an external course enough evidence?
faqs.a: It shows the course was completed. Auditors may still ask how you evaluated whether the person applies what was learned, because the APG paper says participation alone does not necessarily demonstrate competence. Pair certificates with observation, work review, or assessment results.

faqs.q: Are APG papers binding on certification bodies?
faqs.a: No. The APG states its papers reflect different views in management system auditing, are not intended as specified requirements or criteria all auditors must follow, and have not been endorsed by ISO, ISO/TC 176, or the IAF. They are still the most detailed public description of how auditors approach competence.

factCheck.claim: APG is an informal group drawn from ISO/TC 176 and IAF; papers not definitive, not requirements, not endorsed by ISO, TC 176 or IAF; list includes Competence, Evidence collection, Two-stage initial certification audit.

APG Competence paper edition 2 2022-06-01: auditor should assess process for determining competences, observe determination, review actions and effectiveness evaluation; competence evaluated within all QMS processes; share in daily team meetings; 7.2 d 'appropriate' documented information gives leeway; production/service sampling opportunities (interview process leaders/HR, observe performance, interview sample, confirm able to perform, verify replacements); PDCA figure examples; actions list; participation alone not evidence of competence; records examples; monitoring for maintenance; caution on documented information findings; 8.4 external providers; ISO 10015 not audit criteria.

APG Evidence collection: audit evidence generally based on samples; objective evidence does not necessarily depend on documented information except where specified; organization's responsibility to provide objective evidence.

APG Two-stage: stage 1 primarily scoping and planning and readiness; checks documentation in use, internal audits and management reviews; if lacking, inform organization formally to rectify before stage 2.

ISO 9001:2026 published 16 September 2026; harmonized structure retained; new awareness requirements on quality culture and ethical behaviour in 7.3; three year transition; 7.2 not among main changes (reused from ISO 9001 page factCheck).
ISO/IEC 27001 lists 7.2 Competence and 7.3 Awareness; Annex A 6.3; ISO 45001 7.2 includes ability to identify hazards (reused from ISO 27001 and 45001 page factChecks).
